front_blocks.md: What does data protection legislation do?

back_blocks.md: It **protects personal data from being misused**.

cards.front_md: What does data protection legislation do?
cards.back_md: It **protects personal data from being misused**.

front_blocks.md: Give four examples of personal data.

back_blocks.md: **Name**, **address**, **date of birth**, **race** and **religion**.

cards.front_md: Give four examples of personal data.
cards.back_md: **Name**, **address**, **date of birth**, **race** and **religion**.

front_blocks.md: Under the data protection principles, what must personal data be collected for?

back_blocks.md: **Specified and lawful purposes** — an organisation **cannot use personal data for any purpose other than the one it originally stated**, and cannot pass it on without permission.

cards.front_md: Under the data protection principles, what must personal data be collected for?
cards.back_md: **Specified and lawful purposes** — an organisation **cannot use personal data for any purpose other than the one it originally stated**, and cannot pass it on without permission.

front_blocks.md: Why can a bank not ask a new customer about their previous trips?

back_blocks.md: Personal data must be **adequate, relevant and not excessive**, so an organisation **cannot request personal data it does not need right away**.

cards.front_md: Why can a bank not ask a new customer about their previous trips?
cards.back_md: Personal data must be **adequate, relevant and not excessive**, so an organisation **cannot request personal data it does not need right away**.

front_blocks.md: What right does a person have if an organisation holds data about them that is wrong or out of date?

back_blocks.md: Personal data must be **kept accurate and up to date**, so they have a **right to have it corrected or deleted**.

cards.front_md: What right does a person have if an organisation holds data about them that is wrong or out of date?
cards.back_md: Personal data must be **kept accurate and up to date**, so they have a **right to have it corrected or deleted**.

front_blocks.md: What must an organisation do if a person requests the personal data held on them?

front_blocks.md: Name three common exemptions from data protection rules.

back_blocks.md: **Domestic purposes**, such as writing to friends and family or taking pictures for your own enjoyment; **law enforcement**, such as police investigating a crime; and **intelligence services processing**.

cards.front_md: Name three common exemptions from data protection rules.
cards.back_md: **Domestic purposes**, such as writing to friends and family or taking pictures for your own enjoyment; **law enforcement**, such as police investigating a crime; and **intelligence services processing**.

front_blocks.md: What does copyright legislation protect?

back_blocks.md: It protects the **intellectual property of an individual or a company**, making it **illegal to copy, modify or distribute** software or other intellectual property **without the relevant permission**.

cards.front_md: What does copyright legislation protect?
cards.back_md: It protects the **intellectual property of an individual or a company**, making it **illegal to copy, modify or distribute** software or other intellectual property **without the relevant permission**.

front_blocks.md: When is copyright applied to an original work, and how long does it last?

back_blocks.md: Copyright is **automatically applied** to original work and does not expire until **25 to 70 years from the death of the creator**, depending on the type of work.

cards.front_md: When is copyright applied to an original work, and how long does it last?
cards.back_md: Copyright is **automatically applied** to original work and does not expire until **25 to 70 years from the death of the creator**, depending on the type of work.

front_blocks.md: Whose responsibility is it to act when a work has been copied?

back_blocks.md: It is the **creator's own responsibility** to take action.

cards.front_md: Whose responsibility is it to act when a work has been copied?
cards.back_md: It is the **creator's own responsibility** to take action.

front_blocks.md: Name three primary breaches of copyright.

back_blocks.md: **Copying an original work**, **issuing a copy to the public**, **renting or lending a copy to the public**, **performing, showing or playing the work in public**, and **making an adaptation** of it.

cards.front_md: Name three primary breaches of copyright.
cards.back_md: **Copying an original work**, **issuing a copy to the public**, **renting or lending a copy to the public**, **performing, showing or playing the work in public**, and **making an adaptation** of it.

front_blocks.md: Define **software piracy**.

back_blocks.md: Software piracy is the **illegal copying and distribution of software**.

cards.front_md: Define **software piracy**.

front_blocks.md: Name three methods companies use to prevent software piracy.

back_blocks.md: A **product key or licence** to activate the software, an **agreement of terms and conditions** the user must accept before installing, and **holograms** on packaging that are too difficult and costly for pirates to copy.

cards.front_md: Name three methods companies use to prevent software piracy.
cards.back_md: A **product key or licence** to activate the software, an **agreement of terms and conditions** the user must accept before installing, and **holograms** on packaging that are too difficult and costly for pirates to copy.

front_blocks.md: Give three examples of a copyright exemption.

back_blocks.md: Uses **for the benefit of people with a disability**, **non-commercial research or private study**, **recordings of broadcasts for archiving**, **copies made by a library, educational establishment, museum or archive**, and use in a **parody**.

cards.front_md: Give three examples of a copyright exemption.

front_blocks.md: Name four ways an individual can be monitored using digital technology.

back_blocks.md: **CCTV**, **automatic number plate recognition (ANPR)**, **physical forms of identification**, **network activity** such as IP and MAC addresses, **GPS data shared by apps**, and **GPS trackers**.

cards.back_md: **CCTV**, **automatic number plate recognition (ANPR)**, **physical forms of identification**, **network activity** such as IP and MAC addresses, **GPS data shared by apps**, and **GPS trackers**.

front_blocks.md: Name four health issues caused by prolonged use of IT.

cards.front_md: Name four health issues caused by prolonged use of IT.

front_blocks.md: What causes repetitive strain injury?

back_blocks.md: Damage to the **fingers, wrists and joints**, traditionally caused by **prolonged use of a keyboard and mouse**.

cards.front_md: What causes repetitive strain injury?
cards.back_md: Damage to the **fingers, wrists and joints**, traditionally caused by **prolonged use of a keyboard and mouse**.

front_blocks.md: Give three ways to prevent repetitive strain injury.

back_blocks.md: Have the **correct posture**, **use a wrist support** if necessary, **take regular breaks**, and make use of **ergonomic keyboards**.

cards.front_md: Give three ways to prevent repetitive strain injury.

front_blocks.md: What causes eye strain?

cards.front_md: What causes eye strain?

back_blocks.md: **Take regular breaks**, use an **anti-glare screen filter**, and **change from a CRT to an LCD monitor**.

front_blocks.md: Define **physical safety**.

back_blocks.md: Physical safety is **creating a safe environment when using technology**, considering dangers that could lead to **serious injury or loss of life** and identifying strategies to mitigate them.

cards.front_md: Define **physical safety**.

front_blocks.md: Name four physical safety risks of using ICT.

back_blocks.md: **Electrocution** from spilling drinks near electrical equipment, **fire hazard** from overloading plug sockets, **equipment overheating**, **trailing cables** as a trip hazard, and **heavy equipment falling**.

cards.front_md: Name four physical safety risks of using ICT.
cards.back_md: **Electrocution** from spilling drinks near electrical equipment, **fire hazard** from overloading plug sockets, **equipment overheating**, **trailing cables** as a trip hazard, and **heavy equipment falling**.

front_blocks.md: Give three ways to reduce the risk of electrocution.

back_blocks.md: **Keep liquids away** from electrical equipment, ensure cables are **properly insulated and protected**, **turn off and unplug equipment before cleaning or maintenance**, and use **circuit breakers or fuses** to prevent electrical overload.

cards.front_md: Give three ways to reduce the risk of electrocution.

front_blocks.md: Give three ways to reduce the risk of fire from overloaded sockets.

back_blocks.md: Use **surge protectors**, ensure there are **enough plug sockets** in the room, **do not plug too many devices into the same socket**, and **do not leave devices plugged in and unattended**.

cards.front_md: Give three ways to reduce the risk of fire from overloaded sockets.
cards.back_md: Use **surge protectors**, ensure there are **enough plug sockets** in the room, **do not plug too many devices into the same socket**, and **do not leave devices plugged in and unattended**.

front_blocks.md: Give three ways to stop equipment overheating.

back_blocks.md: Ensure equipment is **properly ventilated and not obstructed**, keep **flammable materials away from heat sources**, **do not cover air vents**, and **regularly check equipment** for signs of wear or damage.

cards.front_md: Give three ways to stop equipment overheating.
